investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (all VM slots consumed or at limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (all VM slots consumed or at limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~141–154 s across all three checks). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever calling createAgent, meaning no runtime evidence can be produced and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is fully missing.
